title: The Hidden Ocean
narration: Beneath a cracked shell of ice, an ocean holds twice the water of all Earth's oceans combined. Could something move in that dark water? We have never seen it, yet it may hold life.
visual_goal: Close-up of Europa's icy surface cracking, revealing a dark ocean below

title: Galileo's Discovery
narration: In January one thousand six hundred ten, Galileo Galilei spotted a tiny dot orbiting Jupiter. He thought it was a star. That faint dot would reveal an ocean world, reshaping our search for life.
visual_goal: Old telescope view of Jupiter and its moons, then Galileo's sketch

title: The Icy Shell
narration: Europa's surface is a brilliant white shell, bouncing back sixty-seven percent of sunlight. But beneath, temperatures plunge to minus one hundred sixty degrees Celsius, yet a hidden ocean flows.
visual_goal: Bright icy surface with cracks, reflecting sunlight

title: Tidal Lock
narration: Europa is gravitationally locked with Jupiter; one side always faces the planet. That constant pull squeezes its insides, generating heat that keeps the ocean liquid.
visual_goal: Europa orbiting Jupiter, always showing same face, with tidal bulges

title: The Magnetic Clue
narration: In the late 1990s, the Galileo spacecraft detected something conductive beneath the ice. It was as if the ocean itself was breathing, shifting with Jupiter's pull.
visual_goal: Spacecraft measuring magnetic field lines around Europa

title: Ocean's Depth
narration: That hidden ocean is sixty to one hundred fifty kilometers deep, far deeper than any Earth ocean, like stacking ten Mariana Trenches end to end.
visual_goal: Cross-section of Europa showing thick ice and deep ocean

title: Juno's Flyby
narration: In two thousand twenty-two, NASA's Juno spacecraft flew within three hundred fifty-two kilometers of Europa, revealing its fractured face filled with chaos and promise.
visual_goal: Juno spacecraft flying past Europa, surface details rushing by

title: A Day on Europa
narration: A day on Europa lasts three point five five Earth days, each slow rotation offering a new angle on the frozen enigma.
visual_goal: Time-lapse of Europa rotating against starfield

title: The Clipper Arrives
narration: The Europa Clipper launched in two thousand twenty-four to study that ocean. Dozens of flybys will peel back layers, bringing us closer to understanding that hidden ocean.
visual_goal: Europa Clipper spacecraft flying over Europa's surface with instruments

title: The Final Question
narration: Could something live in that alien ocean? Scientists think Europa is a promising place. The answer might redefine our place in the universe, and the only way to find out is to go.
visual_goal: Europa's ocean with hypothetical life forms, then question mark fading in
